eligibility.quote:
ROS log gets somehow horribly mangled
And prevents Ctrl+C to work.
Strange thing is that it happens only sometimes.

loudness.quote:
If block() is called without initializing serial, it uses default value for file_descriptor in serial_pos.cpp:line 320. Which I think causes the problem.

```
    tcsetattr(file_descriptor, TCSAFLUSH, &options);
```

resolution.quote:
Thus, the proposed patch is going to call serial.block() function after serial.open() in kobuki.cpp
Also, ecl serial.block() should warn user if file_descriptor is not initialized.

notes: Verified via gh api: issue #272 body (mangled log, Ctrl+C dead, intermittent) and jihoonl's diagnosis comment-21917240 in full, including the code excerpt with serial.block(4000) preceding serial.open(...), the 0.3.9 comparison, the serial_pos.hpp line-153 documentation reference, and the tcsetattr on an uninitialised file_descriptor at serial_pos.cpp:320. Eligible at step 6 (library API): a documented call-order precondition of the provider's ecl::Serial API violated by the consumer is a timing/order failure crossing the library boundary, and with the consumer that opened first (0.3.9) the same provider works. Class 'other' agreed (no listed class names a call-order precondition). Silent agreed, and detection_stage 'activate' is the right reading since the misuse runs in Kobuki::init during node start-up; the maintainer's own wish ('ecl serial.block() should warn user if file_descriptor is not initialized') confirms no existing diagnostic fired. Resolution 'recommended' agreed: the patch was proposed and merged (PR #278), but the source shows no run of the fixed composition; the 'working fine' observation belongs to the older 0.3.9 consumer, which the schema counts as evidence for a recommended status, not observed.
